newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil gains on IPE, premiums steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil gains on IPE, premiums steady.

text.p: NWE gas oil rose on Wednesday with IPE futures and spot premiums were steady, but diesel maintained a huge premium to the 0.2 percent sulphur market, traders said.
Nov IPE gained $3.50 at $234.00 a tonne, reacting to American Petroleum Institute (API) data showing heating oil stocks in the U.S. Northeast fell 917,000 barrels last week.
Heating oil cargoes were bid at Nov IPE +$7, countered by offers at +$10, steady on Tuesday's traded levels.
After Tuesday's Russian trades at Nov IPE +$3.50 and +$5.50 cif NWE, one dealer offered a Russian cargo at Nov IPE +$3.25, but others valued the grade at nearer Nov +$4/$6.

Traders differed on the fundamental gas oil supply situation. Many of the U.S. cargoes fixed to come to Europe have yet to arrive in the region and some anticipated more pressure on prices. But others questioned this view:
"There is enough oil for the next couple of days of trade but the question is whether there will be enough for the whole winter," one trader said.
On the barge market, intermediate grade low sulphur barge premiums were steady at around Nov IPE +$33/35 fob ARA.
Heating oil was steady around $6/7 for refinery grade and $5/5.50 for storage.
